title: FIFO
description: Calculate ending inventory and cost of goods sold using first-in, first-out.
html:
What does FIFO mean?

FIFO means First-In, First-Out.

The earliest inventory costs are assigned to Cost of Goods Sold first.

Therefore, ending inventory generally contains the most recent inventory costs.

Example

Assume a company has:

100 units @ $10 $1,000
100 units @ $12 $1,200
Total: 200 units $2,200

Suppose the company sells 150 units.

FIFO Cost of Goods Sold

FIFO assumes the oldest units are sold first.

100 units × $10 $1,000
50 units × $12 $600
FIFO COGS $1,600

Ending Inventory

There are 50 units remaining from the newest purchase.

50 × $12 = $600 Ending Inventory

FIFO pattern

  • Oldest costs → COGS
  • Newest costs → Ending Inventory

quiz.prompt: A company has 100 units at $20 and then buys 100 units at $25. If 120 units are sold using FIFO, what is COGS?
quiz.explanation: FIFO assigns the first 100 units at $20 ($2,000) plus 20 units at $25 ($500), for total COGS of $2,500.
